Redheffer's machine

The impostors
Motion

The claim

Charles Redheffer charged the people of Philadelphia to see a machine that ran by itself. Weights in two boxes pressed on ramps set at 45 degrees and, he said, pushed a horizontal wheel round without end. He asked the state for money to build a bigger one.

What really drives it

The engineer sent to inspect it noticed that the teeth of the gears were worn on the wrong side. The small gear that the machine was supposed to drive was in fact driving the machine. When Redheffer took the show to New York, Robert Fulton pulled away some boards and followed a catgut cord to an upper room, where an old man sat turning a crank.
